name: AEON

source.quote: AEON represents a state-of-the-art, industrially bespoke humanoid.
Auto-swap for continuous work; each charge lasts up to 4 hours

timeline.detail: Hexagon launched AEON at its Hexagon LIVE Global 2025 event in Las Vegas, positioning it for manipulation, asset inspection, reality capture and operator support in automotive, aerospace, manufacturing and logistics.

source.quote: AEON represents a state-of-the-art, industrially bespoke humanoid.

timeline.detail: Hexagon named Schaeffler and Pilatus as pilot partners evaluating AEON for manipulation, machine tending, part inspection and other use cases; this is a named-partner pilot commitment, not a completed named-customer delivery.

source.quote: Schaeffler - piloting AEON for manipulation, machine tending, part inspection

notes: AEON is not sold publicly; Hexagon states it is deployed only through enterprise pilot partnerships (named: Schaeffler, Pilatus; BMW is cited by several secondary aggregator sites but was not confirmed on Hexagon's own pages during this build). No price has been published, so price_history is left empty rather than using the speculative ~$20,000 figure some aggregators cite.

A November 2025 Hexagon press item (via Microsoft Ignite 2025 coverage) states AEON 'completed more than 1,600 missions without interruption' during pilot testing — evidence of extended demonstrated operation at partner sites, but not tied to a single uncut video or named unit delivery, so delivery.status is kept at 'claimed' rather than 'demonstrated' or 'shipped'.
walking_speed_kmh is converted from the manufacturer's stated 2.4 m/s (→ 8.64 km/h, rounded to 8.6 km/h).
